v.why: The residual skip on 0->3 is hugely beneficial in conv-based cells (exp 3) but harmful in pooling-dominated cells (exp 4).
Removing the input-output skip from a deep conv cell cripples trainability (exps 11, 12), whereas pool-heavy cells do not benefit from the skip.
Without the 0->3 residual, cutting edge 0 removes a major signal path and costs far more (exp 18 vs 17).
If node 2 receives little or no input, a conv on 2->3 has almost nothing to transform (exp 1 vs 2).
With 0->2 removed, node 2 carries less information, so the conv on edge 5 contributes less (exp 1 vs 2).
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a conv adds capacity, while replacing a 3x3 conv with a 1x1 is roughly neutral (exp 16 vs 15).
When node 1's outgoing edges are sparse, upgrading 0->1 to a conv has less path to the output (exp 5 vs 6).
When 0->2 is absent, replacing the only conv into node 2 with a skip removes more capacity (exp 13 vs 14).
In sparse cells with few conv paths, adding a conv on 0->3 provides badly needed capacity (exp 20), whereas in dense conv cells it displaces the crucial skip (exp 19).
In pooling-dominated cells, adding an identity bypass gives a shallow, low-capacity network and hurts accuracy (exp 4), unlike in conv cells (exp 3).

Here are 10 hypotheses. Each is grounded in the 20 experiments where they give direct evidence, and in known NAS-Bench-201 structure where they don't.

**Patterns in the experiments**

- **The skip on edge 3 interacts with the rest of the cell.**
  - In an all-conv cell, adding the skip gains up to +16 pts on IN16 (exp 3), and removing it costs about the same (exps 11, 12).
  - In an all-pool cell, adding the skip hurts badly on C10 and C100, about −18 pts (exp 4).
- **Some edits have no path to the output.** A conv edit gives almost nothing when its source or destination node is cut off.
  - Edge 5 adds little when node 2 receives nothing because e1 and e2 are none (exp 1 vs 2).
  - Edge 0 adds little when node 1's outgoing edges are sparse (exp 5 vs 6).
- **Removing an edge hurts more when there is no residual.** Removing edge 0 costs much more when edge 3 is none (exp 18 vs 17).
- **What gets replaced matters.** Putting a conv on edge 5 helps much more when it replaces avg_pool than when it replaces nor_conv_3x3 (exp 16 vs 15).
- **Redundant paths cushion edits.** Changing edge 2 to skip hurts more when edge 1 is none, because node 2 then has no other conv path (exp 13 vs 14).
- **A conv path matters most in a near-empty cell.** Adding a conv on edge 3 when the cell is otherwise empty gives large gains (exp 20).
